title: DFA: Set of strings ending at 'b' from alphabet {a, b}
question: 7a. DFA: Set of strings ending at 'b' from alphabet {a, b}.
theory: A Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) consists of states and transition rules. For strings ending in 'b', the DFA starts in q0 (not ending in 'b'). If it reads 'a', it stays in q0. If it reads 'b', it transitions to q1 (ending in 'b', accepting state). From q1, reading 'a' goes back to q0, while 'b' stays in q1.
algorithm: Define transition logic where state q0 is initial/reject and q1 is accepting.
Read each character of the input string sequentially.
If character is 'a', transition current state to q0; if 'b', transition to q1.
After processing all characters, check if the final state is q1.
Accept the string if final state is q1, otherwise reject.
output:
DFA Simulation (Ends in 'b' over {a, b}):
String: ab    -> Accepted
String: aab   -> Accepted
String: ba    -> Rejected
String: b     -> Accepted
String: aba   -> Rejected
